Louisville’s Lifestyle, Legacy and Real Estate Magazine

Keys and Kentucky Bourbon is a digital magazine for people who love this city — its homes, its bourbon, its tables, its traditions, and the businesses that keep Louisville moving. This media kit introduces the placements available to advertisers in our inaugural editions.

The Publication

One magazine, read the Louisville way

Every edition moves through the departments our readers come back for — Real Estate Watch, Bourbon and Business, Culture and Community, Dining and Lifestyle, Lifestyle Spotlight, Racing and Events, and Louisville Greats. Your business appears inside that reading experience, beside the stories Louisville is already opening.

⌂

Homes and Real Estate

Readers following Louisville neighborhoods, market movement, and the path from dreaming about a home to holding the keys.

❧

Bourbon Culture

Distilleries, founders, and the craft and business of Kentucky bourbon — the spirit that carries Louisville’s name around the world.

✦

Dining, Nightlife and Racing

Restaurants, lounges, Churchill Downs, and the events calendar that fills Louisville weekends for residents and visitors alike.

⚜

Community and Legacy

Local entrepreneurs, neighborhood institutions, and the Louisville greats whose work still shapes the city today.

Advertising Opportunities

Four ways into the edition

Every placement is priced per edition on our published rate card below, so you can choose the position that fits your business — and we will match it to the right edition and department.

No. 1

Featured Business Profile

A full editorial-style profile of your business inside the department where it belongs — your story, your people, and what sets you apart, presented with the same care as our editorial features.

  • Full-length profile written in magazine style
  • Your business card or logo presented in full
  • Direct link to your website
No. 2

Digital Display Advertising

Display placements woven into the reading flow of the magazine’s departments, plus a position on the Business Card Showcase — our signature page of Louisville businesses, presented in gold on black.

  • In-article display positions within departments
  • Business Card Showcase slots
  • Every placement links to your business
Always labeled Sponsored No. 3

Sponsored Editorial

A story your business sponsors — an opening, an anniversary, a craft worth explaining — produced to magazine standard and clearly identified as sponsored wherever it appears. Our readers’ trust is the product; we protect it openly.

  • Produced with our editorial team
  • Clearly labeled “Sponsored” in every placement
  • Placed within a relevant department
No. 4

Premium and Recurring Placements

The positions readers see first — cover-adjacent and contents-page placements — and recurring monthly advertising that keeps your business present edition after edition as the magazine grows.

  • Cover-adjacent and contents-page positions
  • Recurring monthly presence across editions
  • First consideration as new placements open

The Inquiry Process

From first email to live in the edition

1

Reach Out

Email keysandkentuckybourbon@gmail.com with your business name and the placement you are interested in.

2

Receive Your Placement Plan

We reply with a placement plan matched to your business, your department, and the edition calendar — including the package details for your review.

3

Approve the Proof

You see your placement exactly as readers will — profile, display, or showcase card — and approve the proof before anything publishes.

4

Go Live in the Edition

Your business appears in the edition, in front of Louisville readers, with your link live from the first day of publication.

Two doors, kept separate

This page is the advertising door. If you are writing about advertising, sponsorship, or a featured profile, use the form here or email us directly — your message goes to our advertising desk.

Readers and subscribers take the other door: Founding Reader and subscription inquiries go to info@keysandkentuckybourbon.com, so reader mail is never mixed with advertising.
